proposals.observation: Of 11 quiz sessions in the 48-hour window, 9 dropped at intro_load — before a single question appeared. Only 1 person reached email_shown and 1 reached q1_shown. Zero completions. The abandonment is not happening at a hard question or an email gate. It is happening before the quiz has communicated any reason to stay. The intro screen is almost certainly the only thing those 9 people saw.
proposals.proposal: The intro page needs a concrete, specific hook in the first two visible sentences — something that tells the reader exactly what they will learn about themselves and why it is worth 90 seconds of their time. Current intro copy (see CURRENT_TEXT) opens with a generic framing that could sit on any personality quiz. Replace it with copy grounded in the one thing Joel's ICP already feels: they earn well, they have read the books, and the number in their account still does not move. Name that specific experience before asking them to do anything.
proposals.current_text:
Discover your money personality

Take this short quiz to understand the beliefs that are quietly shaping your financial decisions — and what to do about them.
proposals.new_text:
Why does the money not stick?

You earn well. You have read at least one book about this. And yet the number in your account at the end of the month is not what it should be. This quiz names the specific belief pattern underneath that — in about 90 seconds.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate toward Vigilance baseline
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation opens at 66.67% across 12 sends. The Money Worship automation opens at 37.5% across 16 sends — a 29-point gap on a larger send volume. Both automations are triggered by the same quiz, so the audience quality is comparable. The gap is most likely in the subject line or preview text of the Worship sequence's first email, not in the content itself, because open rate is decided before the email is read.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line and preview text of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject line (see CURRENT_TEXT) is abstract and self-referential. The Vigilance sequence's equivalent line is concrete and slightly uncomfortable, which is why people open it. The Worship replacement should name the specific behaviour — spending as proof, the purchase that felt like a decision — rather than labelling the personality type back at the reader.
proposals.current_text:
subject: Your money personality result: Money Worship
preview: Here's what it means for you and your finances.
proposals.new_text:
subject: The purchase that felt like a plan
preview: You did not buy that thing impulsively. You bought it because spending felt like forward motion. Here is what that pattern is costing you.

proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed on 2026-09-03: "Daily Blog Post" at 08:03 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 13:00. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published — meaning the pipeline is nearly empty and the one queued post is not reaching the site while the workflow is broken. With zero quiz completions feeding the email list and a broken blog workflow, there is no organic re-engagement path running today.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow run log and fix the failing step. The blocked-paths rule prevents edits to .github/workflows/* directly, so this proposal targets the most likely root cause: the content file the workflow is trying to process. Failed blog workflows at this stage of a nearly-empty queue typically mean the workflow is trying to read a queue file or front-matter field that is malformed or missing in the one remaining queued post. Validate and correct the queued post's front-matter so the workflow has a clean file to process on its next run.
